In 2025, the Company recorded other operating charges of $ 1,261 million. These charges consisted of $ 960 million related to the impairment of our BodyArmor trademark which impacted our North America operating segment... $ 44 million related to the impairment of a trademark in our Latin America operating segment, $ 41 million related to the impairment of a trademark and property, plant and equipment in our Asia Pacific operating segment

During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company recorded asset impairment charges of $ 44 million and $ 126 million, respectively, related to a trademark in Latin America. These impairment charges were derived using Level 3 inputs and were primarily driven by revised projections of future operating results and changes in macroeconomic conditions. These charges were recorded in the line item other operating charges in our consolidated statements of income.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded an asset impairment charge of $ 29 million related to a trademark in Asia Pacific and an asset impairment charge of $ 12 million related to the fixed assets of this business. These impairment charges were derived using Level 3 inputs and were primarily driven by revised projections of future operating results. These charges were recorded in the line item other operating charges in our consolidated statement of income.

input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges, the initial verdict of SUPPORTED is confirmed and strengthened.

Challenge H1 (whether trademark impairments reduced operating income) is REFUTED. The evidence clearly shows that trademark impairment charges were recorded in "other operating charges" which is a line item that reduces operating income. Evidence E8, E9, and E11 all explicitly state that trademark impairments were recorded in "other operating charges in our consolidated statement(s) of income."

Challenge H2 (whether impairments were reversed) found NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE of any reversal or adjustment that would negate the impact on full-year 2025 operating income.

Challenge H3 (whether the impairment occurred in 2024 instead of 2025) is REFUTED. Evidence E13 explicitly states the $31 million trademark impairment in Latin America occurred "During the three and six months ended June 27, 2025." Evidence E10 confirms that in 2025, there was a $44 million impairment (compared to $126 million in 2024) for a Latin America trademark.

The new evidence from the 10-K for full year 2025 (E9, E10, E11, E12) provides even stronger support than the initial Q2 evidence. These passages confirm that during the full year ended December 31, 2025, Coca-Cola recorded multiple trademark impairment charges that reduced operating income:
- $960 million for BodyArmor trademark (North America)
- $44 million for a trademark in Latin America
- $29 million for a trademark in Asia Pacific (part of the $41 million charge)

All of these were recorded in "other operating charges" which reduces operating income. The evidence review confirms E12 as ENTAILS with EXACT_MATCH period compatibility and HISTORICAL_FACT statement time, making it valid evidence for the full year 2025 claim.
